title: Smorrebrod with Herring
subtitle: Danish open sandwich with herring and dill cream
excerpt: Pickled herring fillets are arranged on thickly buttered dark rye bread with onion rings and a dill soured cream. Smorrebrod is Denmark's art form of the open sandwich. The herring version is the oldest and most traditional of all. No cooking required -- assembly is everything.
sourceNotes: Smorrebrod means 'buttered bread'. The Danish open sandwich is an art form -- precise layers of toppings on a single slice of dense rye bread. Pickled herring is the most traditional topping, eaten at lunch across Denmark.

content.text: Smorrebrod is assembled in layers and eaten with a knife and fork -- it is not a sandwich in the hand-held sense. The thick butter layer protects the bread from the wet toppings. Serve immediately after assembling.

items.prepNote: use pickled herring fillets -- sold in jars in the pickles aisle
use 2 slices of dense dark rye bread -- not wheat bread

content.text: Spread softened butter thickly and evenly on each slice of rye bread.
Mix soured cream with a squeeze of lemon juice and a small handful of chopped dill.
Arrange herring fillets neatly on the buttered bread. Place onion rings on top.
Spoon the dill cream over the top. Finish with more fresh dill. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Wet toppings applied directly without butter
items.fix: Butter the bread generously first -- it acts as a barrier. Serve immediately after assembly.

content.text: Denmark. Eaten at lunch in offices, schools, and restaurants. The herring version is the oldest and most traditional smorrebrod. Accompanied by a cold beer or a small glass of aquavit.
